a: An application that brings programming tools together
tasks.fb: The IDE supports programming. It is not itself the source language.

tasks.q: Match each facility to its purpose.
tasks.fb: These facilities work together within the development environment.

tasks.q: Match the editor feature to the benefit.
pairs: Makes code elements easier to distinguish
tasks.fb: Editing support improves productivity and readability, but programmers still need to check their code.

tasks.q: Does syntax highlighting prove that a calculation is correct?
a: No, it mainly helps distinguish code elements
Yes, all coloured code is correct
Yes, if every line is blue
Only when the font is large
tasks.fb: Colour is a reading aid. It does not prove the algorithm gives the intended result.

tasks.q: Which facility lets you start the program and see its output?
tasks.fb: The IDE invokes its configured execution tools and displays the results.

tasks.q: Where would you look to see the result of print(6 * 4)?
tasks.fb: The statement sends 24 to the output area.

tasks.q: Which repair addresses the visible syntax error on line 4?
a: Add the closing ) after the string
tasks.fb: The opening bracket needs a matching closing bracket.

tasks.q: Select TWO sensible uses of diagnostics.
opts: Read the message to identify the kind of problem
Assume the IDE repairs every fault automatically
Inspect nearby lines as well as the highlighted one
Ignore testing once the message disappears
correct: Read the message to identify the kind of problem
Inspect nearby lines as well as the highlighted one
tasks.fb: Diagnostics guide investigation. The reported location may be where a problem was noticed.

tasks.q: Execution pauses before the calculation. What should you do to inspect its result?
a: Step over it, then inspect total
tasks.fb: A breakpoint pauses before the line. Stepping lets you see the effect of executing it.

tasks.q: Match the debugging action to its use.
pairs: Execute a line and pause again
tasks.fb: Use the facilities together to investigate where actual behaviour diverges from your expectation.

tasks.q: Which replacement meets the stated requirement?
tasks.fb: Multiplying the unit price by the quantity calculates the bill.

tasks.q: Which is the strongest follow-up after the repair?
a: Run the original test and another known case
Assume one edit fixed every possible fault
Check only that the source is coloured
tasks.fb: Retesting checks the repair. More than one known case gives better evidence.

tasks.q: Select the useful IDE facility for each need.
pairs: Reduce typing of a long variable name
Stop just before an incorrect calculation
See a message about a missing bracket
tasks.fb: Choose the facility that directly addresses the programmer’s next step.

tasks.q: A debugger shows correct inputs but the wrong result after one line. What should happen next?
a: Inspect that calculation, repair it and retest
Assume the debugger caused the fault
tasks.fb: The evidence narrows the investigation to the calculation.

info.title: Tools in one place
info.text:
IDE means integrated development environment.

An IDE combines tools used to create and test programs.

Its facilities may include editing, execution and debugging.

Challenge: Why can bringing these tools together help a programmer?

Different IDEs provide different tools. An editor can be part of an IDE, but a simple text editor alone may not include execution or debugging.

info.title: Writing source code
info.text:
Syntax highlighting uses colour to distinguish code elements.

Auto-completion suggests names or code as you type.

Indentation tools help present blocks clearly.

Challenge: How can auto-completion reduce mistakes without guaranteeing correct code?

Colour meanings vary between themes and IDEs. Recognise what highlighting does rather than memorising one colour scheme.

info.title: Translation and execution
info.text:
An IDE can call a compiler or interpreter.

Run controls start the program using its configured tools.

The output area shows results and may accept input.

Challenge: What is the difference between the editor and the output area?

An IDE may require a separately installed compiler or interpreter. The interface and the language execution tool have different jobs.

info.title: Diagnostic messages
info.text:
Diagnostics identify detected problems in the code.

A message can include a line number and an error description.

Read the surrounding code before deciding on a repair.

Challenge: A message points to line 5. Why might you also inspect line 4?

A warning can differ from an error that prevents execution. Read the message rather than treating every highlight as the same kind of problem.

info.title: Pausing and stepping
info.text:
A breakpoint pauses before a selected line executes.

Step controls advance execution in small steps.

Watching variables reveals how values change.

Challenge: If execution pauses before total = price * quantity, what can you inspect first?

Stepping options differ. Step into can enter a called function, while step over runs that call without stopping on each line inside it.

info.title: Finding a logic error
info.text:
A logic error can remain even when syntax is valid.

Compare actual values with the result you expected.

Retest after changing the faulty statement.

Challenge: The bill should be 24 but is 10. Identify and repair the calculation.

Debugging finds and fixes faults. Testing supplies evidence about whether the program meets its requirements.
